feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
The anti-complexity perspective raises questions about the necessity of supporting OP_CODESEPARATOR, highlighting that its inclusion does not appear to contribute significant value in this context. From a practical standpoint, there is an acknowledgment that wallets are not required to support OP_CODESEPARATOR, which further weakens the argument for maintaining it.
OP_CODESEPARATOR’s relevance is also examined in relation to NOINPUT. The observation is that the existence or absence of OP_CODESEPARATOR does not alter the fundamental properties associated with NOINPUT. It is noted that anyone has the capability to create an output that can be spent using any form of NOINPUT, regardless of whether OP_MASK is implemented or if there is simply no commitment to the input script.
This line of reasoning suggests that OP_CODESEPARATOR may not have a meaningful impact on transaction validation or script execution in scenarios involving NOINPUT, leading to uncertainty about its purpose and utility within these specific technical discussions.
